all_20_argument_preservation_map.source_argument: Use the actual q=1 Schur Weyl-cell simple L_N(μ), μ dominant polynomial, converted from right to left by star. Its highest vector v has weight μ and norm1. The local lemma [F3] proves from the tensorword endomorphism realization that negative coefficient operators span each weight space, positive coefficient operators detect every nonzero vector, and integral cut-root words span every grade whose simple-root coefficients are0or1. It also proves the complete essential-subset basis and the dimension formula  dim L_N(μ)_(μ−α(r,s))=ε_a(r,s),   a_j=μ_j−μ_(j+1). The local lemma [F3] also proves for every dominant a and every interval, by finite matching/path/stack bijections and finite triangular matrix inversion,  ε_a(r,s)=ν_a(r,s)+sum_(u=r+1)^s ε'_a(r,u−1)ν_a(u,s), where ε'_a(r,t)=ε_(a+ω_t)(r,t). These are actual proved local inputs, including all zero dimensions and arbitrary nonrestricted auxiliary weights. [F1, F2, F3, F4, construct]

It also proves the complete essential-subset basis and the dimension formula $\dim L_N(\mu)_{\mu-\alpha(r,s)}=\varepsilon_a(r,s)$, $a_j=\mu_j-\mu_{j+1}$. all_20_argument_preservation_map.retained_argument: Disconnected binary deficit coefficient matrix factors with unchanged separated Cartan coordinates
all_20_argument_preservation_map.source_argument: We spell out a further modular consequence of the same foundation to close the algebraic support seam. Let Γ be a deficit with each simple-root coefficient0or1, with disconnected support Γ=δ+ζ separated by at least one zero coefficient. Take the first component δ entirely inside the Levi on the first N−1 coordinates. Every negative cut word of gradeΓ factors uniquely into a δ-word and a ζ-word, since no root crossing a missing simple root can occur; the two groups commute. Every positive coefficient word of gradeΓ similarly factors. All positive/negative cross commutators between the separated groups vanish. Consequently the matrix of highest coefficients atΓ is the tensor product of the two separate coefficient matrices atδ andζ: for positive tests e,e' and negative words f,f',  highest(e e' f f' v)=highest(e f v) highest(e' f' v). The rightmost separated test/word leaves the Cartan coordinates of the other interval unchanged, since the intervals are nonadjacent; this verifies the displayed equality even though f'f v has shifted weight. [step 1.1, construct]
all_20_argument_preservation_map.formatted_argument: We spell out a further modular consequence of the same foundation to close the algebraic support seam. Let $\Gamma$ be a deficit with each simple-root coefficient $0$ or $1$, with disconnected support $\Gamma=\delta+\zeta$ separated by at least one zero coefficient. Take the first component $\delta$ entirely inside the Levi on the first $N-1$ coordinates. Every negative cut word of grade $\Gamma$ factors uniquely into a $\delta$-word and a $\zeta$-word, since no root crossing a missing simple root can occur; the two groups commute. Every positive coefficient word of grade $\Gamma$ similarly factors. All positive/negative cross commutators between the separated groups vanish. Consequently the matrix of highest coefficients at $\Gamma$ is the tensor product of the two separate coefficient matrices at $\delta$ and $\zeta$: for positive tests $e,e'$ and negative words $f,f'$, $\operatorname{highest}(ee'ff'v)=\operatorname{highest}(efv)\operatorname{highest}(e'f'v)$. The rightmost separated test/word leaves the Cartan coordinates of the other interval unchanged, since the intervals are nonadjacent; this verifies the displayed equality even though $f'fv$ has shifted weight. [step 1.1, construct]

all_20_argument_preservation_map.retained_argument: Dual positive tests and identity on the full component tensor-product weight space
all_20_argument_preservation_map.source_argument: Choose bases f_a v and f'_b v of the separate images. Positive detection yields positive linear-combination tests e_a and e'_b with e_a f_c v=δ_ac v, e'_b f'_d v=δ_bd v, by finite matrix inversion over the field. Thus the products f_a f'_b v are independent, since e_a e'_b tests detect their coefficients; they span by the preceding factorization. On the entire weight space atΓ the operator  P_δ=sum_a f_a e_a is the identity: applied to f_c f'_b v, its cross commutations give f_c f'_b v. Every e_a is a positive Levi coefficient word of nonzero weightδ, and every f_a is a negative Levi coefficient word. This argument proves the identity on arbitrary entangled linear combinations, not only pure products. If a separate image is zero, the full weight space is zero and cannot supply a primitive vector. [step 2.1, construct]

all_20_argument_preservation_map.retained_argument: Disconnected-root primitive exclusion on a composition-series quotient
all_20_argument_preservation_map.source_argument: Now let M0⊂M1 be consecutive terms of a finite composition series of the first level, and choose x∈M1 representing the highest vector of a simple factor, of full deficitΓ. Positive Levi operators of nonzero weight send x into M0, because they annihilate its highest class. If Γ had a disconnected initial componentδ, the identity P_δ x=x would put x intoM0: e_a x∈M0 and f_a preserveM0. This is impossible. Hence any primitive factor vector of binary deficit ending at the last simple root has support a single terminal interval. This is the disconnected-root primitive exclusion, proved here, without a characteristic-zero PBW theorem or a pure-product assumption for x. [step 3.1, construct]

all_20_argument_preservation_map.retained_argument: Every-field descent, scalar extension and composition-factor preservation
all_20_argument_preservation_map.source_argument: The local lemma [F3] uses only the infinite purely transcendental extension K=F(t) for polynomial identities and Gaussian elimination. Its scalar-extension argument is reversible: all cut/raising matrices have entries inF, hence their finite ranks and kernels preserve extension; its essential labels and pivot tests yield bases overF itself. Schur cell simples remain simple under every field extension by the cellular rank-one action and their nonzero form. Extending a finite Schur composition series thus retains the simple factors and their labels, so the integers b_i computed overK are exactly those overF. The first-level weight subspace commutes with extension because it is the image of a finite sum of weight idempotents. Neither an algebraic closure nor an assumption that the original field is infinite is used. All nil/zero-weight cases remain in the equations. [step 8.1, construct]

all_20_argument_preservation_map.formatted_argument: The root normal walk based at $i$ starts with a push for $A$ and scans $u=i+1,\ldots,l$. At coordinates with $a_u=0$ the compensation walk is neutral, even when $B=C=0$: the same position supplies and consumes a compensation slot. At positive coordinates $u$, the last ordinary row $k$ of the width $u$ block gives a removable node, and $C(i,u)=u-i+\sum_{t=i}^{u-1}a_t=u-\lambda_j+j-k$. Thus $C(i,u)=0$ is exactly the removable node's residue equal to $A$'s residue. The first ordinary row $k$ of the width $u$ block has an addable node in column $u+1$, and $B(i,u)=u-i+\sum_{t=i}^{u}a_t=u-\lambda_j+j-k+1$. Thus $B(i,u)=0$ is exactly that addable node's residue equal to $A$'s residue. Since $0<a_u<p$ at a positive coordinate, $B=C+a_u$ shows these two events cannot occur together at that same $u$. Empty widths give only the neutral compensation case. The artificial final zero-width row also has no effect. Scanning positive $u$ in increasing order lists the ordinary corners above $A$ in the order $j-1,\ldots,1$, with a width block contributing its boundary event when the residue matches. The top extra addable node of width $\lambda_1+1$ is already the $B$ event of the width $\lambda_1$ coordinate; no boundary event is omitted. [step 10.1, construct]

all_20_argument_preservation_map.retained_argument: Inline q=1 Weyl-to-Murphy corner module and actual right action
all_20_argument_preservation_map.source_argument: Work at q=1 with right Schur modules, reversing the star conversion used for the algebraic count. The Hecke presentation has T_i²=1 and the symmetric-group braid relations; its standard basis T_w maps bijectively to the group basis w, so H(F,1,S_m)=FS_m. Let e be the weight projection of type omega=(1^m), with End_H(H)=H via rho_h(x)=hx. The normalized semistandard map phi_ST is supported from type(T) to type(S). Thus e phi_ST e survives exactly when both types are omega. These tableaux are ordinary standard tableaux, their defining fibers are singleton, and evaluation at1 gives phi_st↦m_st. The higher Schur ideal corner is exactly the higher Murphy ideal, as equality of the corresponding basis spans. The projection on a Weyl cell fixes w_T exactly for type(T)=omega. To read its right H action, choose the independent fixed outer index also of type omega; evaluation at1 then turns phi_st rho_h into m_st h modulo the corresponding higher ideal. Hence W^xi e≅C_M(xi) by w_t↦c_t, with the actual same-shape Murphy action, over every field. [step 13.1, F1, F2, construct]

all_20_argument_preservation_map.retained_argument: Exact lower corner preserves surviving factors and gives signed ordinary restriction multiplicity
all_20_argument_preservation_map.source_argument: Apply the exact lower projection e' to a finite composition series of L_N(mu)p. Each factor L_(N−1)(eta) becomes D_M(eta), proved by the lower-rank form/corner calculation of steps 14.1–15.1; it is a distinctly labelled simple when eta is restricted, and zero otherwise. Deleting repeated terms leaves a composition series of the group restriction corner. Thus the multiplicity of a restricted eta agrees exactly with its lower Schur multiplicity. Nonrestricted eta were retained in the earlier character calculation and are killed only here. For mu=lambda', [F2] gives L_N(mu)e≅D^lambda tensor sign. The candidate nu_i=(lambda\A)' is restricted by the regular-removal hypothesis, and its image is D^(lambda\A) tensor sign. Hence the desired group restriction multiplicity is b_i. Twisting both modules by sign preserves multiplicity because sign of S_n restricts to sign of S_(n−1). To match a left-module convention for the ordinary D in the Statement, apply the exact inverse/star equivalence from right group modules to left ones, g·x=xg^(-1). It commutes with restriction and sign twisting and preserves composition series. The ordinary polytabloid quotient is the same partition-labelled quotient in this convention; if the dictionary uses its contragredient realization, the induced nondegenerate invariant quotient form identifies that simple with its contragredient. Explicitly x↦(y↦beta(x,y)) is bijective and equivariant since beta(gx,y)=beta(x,g^(-1)y). This uses the form only after passing to the nonzero radical quotient, as in [[def-modular-specht-form-and-radical-quotient]]; no self-duality of a possibly degenerate Specht module is assumed. Together with the algebraic count and signature calculation, this gives both displayed cases of the theorem. [step 17.1, F2, F4, construct]

To match a left-module convention for the ordinary $D$ in the Statement, apply the exact inverse/star equivalence from right group modules to left ones, $g\cdot x=xg^{-1}$. The ordinary polytabloid quotient is the same partition-labelled quotient in this convention; if the dictionary uses its contragredient realization, the induced nondegenerate invariant quotient form identifies that simple with its contragredient.
